request: If this is a spanner, the main cutout is too deep which is weakening the tool. Make the cutout shallower by 10mm, but keep the "size" of the spanner the same - meaning the parallel surfaces remain 20mm apart.

actions.operation: Reduce the depth of the main cutout.
actions.relational_constraint: The cutout must be 10 mm shallower than its current depth.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the main cutout in the CAD model and the geometry and direction that define its current depth.
steps: Localize the requested main cutout as the open-ended U-shaped fastener slot in SEC-01, not the shallow upper handle recess in SEC-03. The top, bottom, and top-right isometric views show that this slot is the functional spanner opening, and the stated 20 mm separation corresponds exactly to its opposing inner jaw flats.

Identify the current depth-defining geometry at the closed end of the slot: slot-root flat face 0003 (Brep FACE 18), right slot-root blend face 0002 (Brep FACE 17), and left slot-root blend face 0004 (Brep FACE 19). The slot extends from the open jaw tips toward this root along the longitudinal Z direction.
Identify the adjacent geometry that must be shortened but not laterally repositioned: right inner jaw flat face 0001 (Brep FACE 22) at x=10 and left inner jaw flat face 0005 (Brep FACE 20) at x=-10.

Use the planar upper body land, face 0010 (Brep FACE 24), or an equivalent datum plane parallel to the top view as the sketch plane so that the complete open-jaw profile can be controlled in the X-Z plane.
Project or convert the existing slot edges into the sketch to preserve the current opening location, centerline, and 20 mm jaw width. Retain the two longitudinal side lines at x=10 mm and x=-10 mm.

Create a construction reference from the existing slot-root location and offset the depth-defining root geometry by 10 mm toward the open end of the jaw. This moves the closed end of the U-shaped slot toward the jaw tips and therefore reduces the slot depth by exactly 10 mm.
Reconstruct the transverse slot-root line at the new longitudinal position while keeping it perpendicular to the slot centerline and centered between the two inner jaw flats.

Recreate the two internal root corners with the existing nominal 5 mm radius, tangent to the relocated slot-root line and tangent to the unchanged inner jaw lines. This preserves the stress-relieving rounded-root design rather than introducing sharp internal corners.

Close the profile representing the material between the old and new root locations. Add this volume through the complete 15 mm part thickness, from the continuous lower body face 0014 (Brep FACE 25) to the continuous upper body land 0010 (Brep FACE 24), and Boolean-union it with the wrench body. Equivalently, edit the original U-slot cut sketch and move its root and tangent corner arcs 10 mm toward the open end, then regenerate the through-all cut.

Allow the regeneration to replace or relocate faces 0002, 0003, and 0004 and to trim the root ends of faces 0001 and 0005. Do not modify the large external jaw curves 0000 and 0006 or the open-head transition faces 0009 and 0011.
Confirm that the added material forms a continuous solid with SEC-01 and SEC-02 and that no internal voids, sliver faces, or non-manifold edges remain at the relocated root.

Measure the slot depth along its longitudinal centerline from the same jaw-tip reference used by the original geometry to the new root reference. Verify that the resulting depth is exactly 10 mm less than the original depth.

Inspect the modified root in top, bottom, and isometric views. Verify that the new shallower root increases the load-bearing ligament between the slot and handle, supporting the stated intention to reduce weakening.

actions.operation: Preserve the separation and parallel relationship of the spanner's parallel surfaces.
actions.target: The parallel surfaces that define the stated spanner size.
actions.relational_constraint: The identified surfaces must remain parallel and 20 mm apart after the cutout-depth modification.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the pair of parallel surfaces referred to as defining the spanner's size.
steps: Localize the spanner-size surfaces as right inner jaw flat face 0001 (Brep FACE 22) and left inner jaw flat face 0005 (Brep FACE 20). These are the two opposed planar contact surfaces of the open-ended fastener interface.

Use the longitudinal center plane of the open jaw as the symmetry and dimensional reference. Constrain the right jaw surface to x=10 mm and the left jaw surface to x=-10 mm, or apply equivalent symmetric offsets of 10 mm from the center plane.

Apply or retain a parallel constraint between the two longitudinal jaw-flat sketch lines. Apply a perpendicular 20 mm distance constraint between them so the clear opening remains the specified spanner size.
Do not offset, taper, rotate, draft, or otherwise laterally alter faces 0001 and 0005 while reducing the slot depth. Only shorten their root-end extents where they meet the relocated radius-5 blends.
Maintain tangency between face 0001 and the regenerated right slot-root blend corresponding to face 0002, and between face 0005 and the regenerated left slot-root blend corresponding to face 0004.
Regenerate the model and measure the minimum normal distance between faces 0001 and 0005 at multiple positions along their remaining straight lengths. Confirm a constant value of 20 mm.
Verify that the surface normals of faces 0001 and 0005 are antiparallel and that both surfaces remain parallel to the slot centerline.
Check the jaw opening from the top and bottom views to confirm that the open-end width has not changed and that the relocated root remains centered between the two jaw flats.

Perform an interference or gauge check using a nominal 20 mm-wide rectangular reference body. Confirm that it fits between the parallel jaw flats to the newly reduced slot depth without changing the intended 20 mm spanner size.

intention: Reduce weakening of the tool caused by the excessive cutout depth.
Preserve the spanner's specified size while making the cutout shallower.
